title: REQUIREMENTS ELICITATION AND STAKEHOLDER ANALYSIS
meta: Client Site: Deniz Construction Limited, Ishanyu Bushenyi Road, Mbarara

blocks.text: 1. INTRODUCTION
1.1 Purpose

This document presents the Requirements Elicitation and Stakeholder Analysis conducted for the Deniz Construction Management System (DCMS). It records the empirical data gathered during our site visit, the elicitation techniques used, the challenges encountered, and the current As-Is operational reality of the business.
1.2 Scope

The analysis covers stakeholder identification, power-interest mapping, elicitation techniques applied, field observations, interview findings, documented limitations, and strategic business synthesis to inform the subsequent Requirements Analysis and Specification phase.
1.3 Methodology

Group K applied Direct Observation and Semi-Structured Interviews during a single site visit. Because further follow-up visits were not feasible and the Sales Manager was unwilling to provide further information, this document also establishes the baseline for how unresolvable information gaps are handled through documented business assumptions based on the Ugandan SME context.
1.4 Definitions and Abbreviations

items: As-Is: The current operational state of the business before system implementation
DCMS: Deniz Construction Management System
MoMo: Mobile Money
SME: Small and Medium Enterprise
SRS: Software Requirements Specification
URA: Uganda Revenue Authority

blocks.text: 1.5 References

items: IEEE Std 830-1998 - Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications
SWE2102 Course Allocation - Group K, Requirements Engineering

blocks.text: 1.6 Document Overview

Section 2 provides the Business Context. Section 3 states the Problem Statement. Section 4 covers Stakeholder Analysis. Section 5 details Elicitation Techniques and Field Realities. Section 6 documents Challenges and Limitations. Section 7 presents Strategic Business Synthesis. Section 8 concludes and transitions to the next phase.
2. BUSINESS CONTEXT

Deniz Construction Limited is a small construction materials business located on Ishanyu-Bushenyi Road, Mbarara, Uganda. The business produces and sells concrete blocks, pavers and kerbs. Operations are highly centralised, a single Sales Manager acts as supervisor, cashier, payroll distributor, record keeper and tax filer. The Business Owner visits the site daily to review operations and cash. The business operates on a strict no-credit policy with three payment channels: Cash, Mobile Money and Bank Deposit. Physical receipts are printed on-site for customers during truck loading. URA tax filing is done online. No cloud backup exists; records are kept on a single laptop and in physical books. Workers are paid daily in cash without formal contracts.
3. PROBLEM STATEMENT
The current operational model creates several critical vulnerabilities:

items: Super-Manager Bottleneck: One person absorbs supervision, sales, payroll, record keeping and tax filing — a single point of failure.
Unexplained Cash Deficits: End-of-day cash shortages are manually computed without a tool to log operational expenses (e.g. loader lunch, transport), making variance causes opaque.
Informal Labour Practices: Attendance relies entirely on the Sales Manager's memory; no formal attendance tracking exists, enabling ghost-worker risk.
Data Vulnerability: All digital records reside on a single laptop with no cloud backup; physical receipts and books provide limited redundancy.
Manual Reconciliation Burden: The Sales Manager uses the PC in the evening to process deficits and prepare summaries for the Owner — a heavy, error-prone manual workload.

blocks.text: 4. STAKEHOLDER ANALYSIS

The organisational structure is highly flattened. Roles are heavily concentrated, so the traditional corporate hierarchy does not apply. We mapped stakeholders on a Power and Interest grid to determine engagement strategy and identify critical data gaps.
4.1 Stakeholder Identification and Power Interest Mapping

rows: Strategic oversight. Visits the site daily to review operations and cash.
Manage Closely. Status: Gap. Never interviewed. The system must prioritise the metrics he reviews during his daily evening visits.
The absolute centre of operations. Acts as supervisor, cashier, payroll distributor and record keeper.
Manage Closely. Status: Fact. Interviewed. Acts as the gatekeeper.
Produce blocks and pavers. Paid daily in cash. No formal legal contracts.
Monitor. Status: Gap. No chance to speak to them.
Uganda Revenue Authority. Dictates tax compliance, VAT and receipting standards.
Keep Satisfied. External regulator. No direct engagement but dictates compliance rules.
Purchase blocks and pavers. Pay upfront. Transport their own goods by truck.
Keep Informed. The system must ensure quick processing to minimise loading delays.

blocks.text: 4.2 Common Pitfalls and Engagement Techniques

runs.text: Because the Sales Manager handles almost all operations, she acts as a gatekeeper. She was hesitant to share deep financial workflows, for example, the exact tax calculations and the cash storage arrangements.

We used observation over direct interrogation for sensitive topics. By observing the physical environment, for example, the CCTV cameras, the printer and the laptop usage timing, we inferred security and workflow realities without making her defensive.

blocks.text: 5. ELICITATION TECHNIQUES AND FIELD REALITIES (THE AS-IS STATE)
Group K used Direct Observation and Semi-Structured Interviews. The following facts represent the current operational reality of the business.

items: Workflow and Hardware: The laptop was powered on and actively used during the day. A printer is on site and physical receipts were being printed for customers as trucks loaded.
Logistics: Customers transport their own products by truck. Trucks load in bulk, but the exact counting method (per piece or per pallet) was not visible.
Security: The site has CCTV cameras, indicating a baseline awareness of physical security and cash handling risks.
Machinery: Production area has block-making machinery (vibrators, moulds, mixers) observed on site.
Payment Channels: The business accepts Cash, Mobile Money and direct Bank Deposits.
Credit Policy: The business never gives credit; all payments must be made upfront.
Tax Compliance: The Sales Manager processes taxes online via the URA portal, but the exact manual calculation method was not disclosed.
Pain Points: The Sales Manager explicitly raised insecurity regarding cash handling and stated she uses the PC to process deficits (cash shortages) manually.
Labour: There is no formal attendance system. Attendance relies entirely on the Sales Manager's memory and workers are paid daily in cash without legal contracts.

blocks.text: 6. CHALLENGES IN ELICITATION AND DOCUMENTED LIMITATIONS
As Group K, we faced the following empirical challenges, which are documented as limitations for the project.

items: Stakeholder Hesitance and Information Withholding. The Sales Manager was reluctant to disclose the exact fields on the physical receipts, the method used to calculate URA taxes and the physical cash storage protocols.
Inaccessibility of Secondary Stakeholders. The Business Owner was not available for interview and the Site Workers could not be approached directly.
Incomplete Workflow Visibility. We knew the laptop is used to process deficits, but we could not observe the exact formula or the physical cash reconciliation process.
Further follow-up visits were not feasible. The Sales Manager was unwilling to provide further information and a return visit to the site could not be arranged. The project scope is locked.

blocks.text: 7. STRATEGIC BUSINESS SYNTHESIS

Because we cannot return to the site to close the gaps identified in Section 6, we apply strategic business synthesis. These are logical inferences drawn from verified facts combined with standard operational norms of Ugandan construction SMEs. They serve as baseline implications for the subsequent Requirements Analysis phase.

runs.text: 1. The Nature of Deficits and Cash Insecurity

blocks.text: Fact: The Sales Manager processes deficits manually and cited insecurity (CCTV is present).

Synthesis: In cash-heavy Ugandan SMEs, end-of-day cash shortages are rarely malicious theft. They are almost always caused by unrecorded petty cash expenses (for example, buying lunch for truck loaders or paying for transport) taken directly from the cash drawer.
Implication for Requirements Analysis: The business requires a mechanism to log operational cash-outs to reconcile the physical till against the receipt totals.

Fact: The laptop is on during the day and physical receipts are printed for customers. However, the Sales Manager also heavily utilises the PC right before the Business Owner arrives in the evening specifically to process cash deficits.

Synthesis: The Sales Manager cannot wait until the evening to log sales, because customers require printed receipts immediately upon loading. However, the evening PC usage indicates a distinct, heavy reconciliation burden at the end of the day.

Implication for Requirements Analysis: The future system must support real-time transaction processing and receipt generation during the day, alongside a dedicated, heavy-duty reconciliation workflow for the evening.
Fact: Physical receipts are printed on site and trucks load in bulk. Exact receipt fields are unknown.

Synthesis: To satisfy URA compliance and basic business logic, receipts must contain standard fiscal fields (Sequential ID, Date, VAT, Payment Method). Because clients self-transport and load in bulk, inventory tracking must accommodate flexible units of measure (pieces, pallets, or truckloads).
Implication for Requirements Analysis: The SRS must define flexible unit-of-measure handling and standard receipt fields for URA compliance.

runs.text: 4. Cloud Backup and Remote Access Specification

blocks.text: Fact: The Owner visits the site every day. No cloud backup currently exists.

Synthesis: Because the Owner is physically present daily, a real-time remote monitoring dashboard is operationally redundant. The critical need for cloud technology is strictly for disaster recovery (protecting the single laptop from data loss) and asynchronous historical review.

runs.text: The cloud feature is specified strictly as an Automated Nightly Backup, triggered in the evening after the final reconciliation is complete, to solve the Data Vulnerability problem of relying on a single laptop. The remote portal for the Owner is an Asynchronous Dashboard for reviewing next-day finalised reports and long-term business trends, rather than a live monitoring tool.

blocks.text: 8. CONCLUSION AND TRANSITION
By combining direct observation with logical business synthesis, Group K has mapped the current As-Is state of Deniz Construction Limited and documented all unresolvable elicitation challenges.
All gaps (Workers, Receipt Fields, Cash Storage, Tax Calculation Method) are formally documented as limitations.

This elicitation and stakeholder analysis provides the input for Phase 2: Requirements Analysis and Specification, where the documented facts, synthesis, and implications will be translated into formal Software Requirements (SRS).
